summary: Bend 2.0.35 checker (bend2/bend.ts, "99% human-designed") is a one-pass bidirectional checker over a dependent affine calculus with Type : Type, no universe levels and no positivity check. Consistency rests on a "wall": (1) every live self-call must descend on a strict structural subterm, columns read left to right, EQ until one is LT, erased columns skipped; (2) a live variable is consumed at most once unless bound by a + binder whose type's kind is Data (no function type is Data); (3) dead positions (types, - args, equality endpoints, motives, shadowed/fallback arms) are checked for type only or not visited and may diverge. @unsafe disables descent and the Data wall on + and permits forward/unfilled references; --check-only still prints ALL PROOFS CHECK for a book using one, while --verdict prints SOME PROOFS FAIL naming every def that transitively relies on it. An unfilled law is a dead claim: live use is refused; left open, it counts as a TODO and the CLI refuses the file. bend.ts states its metatheory as "trusted claims"; README says the checker has no proof; the Lean kernel (bendtt.lean, 0 sorry) proves Claim.consistent for BendTT text produced by an unproven elaborator (safe.ts). PROOF.bend beside LAWS.bend must import it (main.ts 809-812; verified by run). Base is exempt from the hole count and the unfilled-law refusal.

facts.claim: The Bend checker header describes the design as two checking modes plus a descent judgment, and names the wall as the sole guard that permits Type : Type, impredicativity and negative recursive types with no universe hierarchy and no positivity check.
facts.quote: this wall permits Type : Type, impredicativity and negative recursive types with no universe hierarchy and no positivity check: omega, Curry and Hurkens each contract a live function-valued binding, and no function type is Data. the gate is the wall.

facts.claim: Exact descent rule as stated in the header: every live self-call descends on a strict subterm in its own case tree, live columns compared EQ left to right, erased columns skipped.
facts.quote: every live self-call descends on a strict subterm in its own case tree, live columns compared EQ left to right, erased columns skipped

facts.claim: The header labels its metatheory as trusted claims, not proofs: subject reduction (by-value only), progress, weak normalization of closed live terms, no closed live inhabitant of Empty.
facts.quote: trusted claims: subject reduction (for by-value reduction), progress, weak normalization of closed live terms, no closed live inhabitant of Empty.

facts.claim: Subject reduction for usage is explicitly narrowed: term substitution does not preserve the measure; the claim covers only weak by-value reduction of closed terms, and three invariants outside the checker (no pass duplicates a term; ownership types are Type not Data; a compiler never adds a copy) carry it.
facts.quote: term-substitution reduction does not preserve the measure ... subject reduction for usage is claimed for weak by-value reduction of closed terms

facts.claim: @unsafe disables three things: self-calls skip descent, binder domains form + at any kind, and it may call an unfilled law or a def below it; the header says the claims do not cover a book that uses one.
facts.quote: an @unsafe def opts out of the wall: its self-calls skip descent, its binder domains form + at any kind, and it calls an unfilled law or a def below it, so the claims above do not cover a book that uses one.

facts.claim: Affine means operationally: a live variable is consumed at most once; a + binder licenses many uses and forms only when its type is Data; quantities None|Lone|Many add sequentially (two live uses saturate to Many) and join pointwise-max across branches; demand is only None or Lone.
facts.quote: a live variable is consumed at most once; a + binder licenses many uses and forms only when its type is Data.

facts.claim: What Data relaxes vs QTT: a Lone Data value may enter a + binder and the callee copies it (certify-once); a function type is Type (a closure captures), an equation is Data (evidence erased); book_valid forbids a function field in Data.
facts.quote: a function type is Type (a closure captures), an equation is Data (evidence is erased) ... a function field never sits in Data

facts.claim: Dead positions and what the checker does with them: a type position, erased (-) argument, equality endpoint or motive checks dead: it may diverge and inhabit Empty; no rule coerces dead to live.
facts.quote: a type position, an erased (-) argument, an equality endpoint or a motive checks dead: it may diverge and inhabit Empty; no rule coerces dead to live.

facts.claim: Holes: ?name fails every check and is shown against the goal; ?TODO alone checks at any goal and marks the book incomplete.
facts.quote: ?TODO alone checks at any goal and marks the book incomplete

facts.claim: term_descend implementation: an erased column (q None) returns EQ (skipped); a Var column is EQ only if the same variable else GT; a Ctr column compares same-constructor fields recursively or searches each field for the argument as a strict subterm (LT); anything else (applications, calls, literals not stepping to a ctor) is GT.
facts.quote: if (q.$ === "None") { return "EQ"; }

Dead (qt None) references are not checked.

facts.claim: The checker comment on infer-ref: a bare or non-shrinking self-reference is an error so a self-reference never escapes as a value; mutual recursion cannot bypass the wall because a forward reference is a live reference to a bodiless def.
facts.quote: a forward reference is a live reference to a bodiless def, which errs (infer-ref) unless the def is @unsafe, so mutual recursion cannot bypass the wall

facts.claim: Check header: demand qt is None (dead) or Lone (live); a dead check measures only None; a binder validates measured <= declared on close and a Lone binder measured Many fails as '(consumed more than once)'; ordinary typing never consults the usage measure.
facts.quote: a Lone binder measured Many (consumed more than once) fails there ... ordinary typing never consults the usage measure

facts.claim: check-mat: a fallback past the datatype's last constructor is replaced by an unvisited Efq (not checked); a live match on a - scrutinee is refused; residue is dead when a live binder in context has an emptied ADT (ctx_dead).

facts.claim: term_check_kind: a + binder's type must fit Kind(Many)=Data; on miss the note printed is 'Note: +x can be used many times, so its type must be Data.'
facts.quote: "Note: +" + k + " can be used many times, so its type must be Data."

facts.claim: book_valid: a final bodiless def that is not Base and not foreign increments book.hols (counted as a TODO); defs declare bodiless up front and define at their event; an ADT's constructor fields are checked against Kind(G) for live fields; there is no positivity check anywhere in book_valid.

facts.claim: Imports: 'import Base' or 'import <path>.bend as Name'; an alias is per-file; a def of an aliased name fills the imported law; cross-file filling is the documented mechanism ('def M.name(..)').
facts.quote: "as Name" binds a per-file alias: Name.x resolves to the file's canonical name, so two aliases of one file agree, and a def of an aliased name fills it.

facts.claim: Halt corpus (36 files): descent rejects any argument that is not a strict structural subterm of its column: HOAS application bod(a2), a def call f(grow(N{})), Nat.sub(d,1n), ndiv(n,2n), a larger literal 7n at a 5n column, a fresh lambda binder, a pure argument swap, a growing accumulator placed before the shrinking column, a nested-match on an earlier binder (parse error), Ann-wrapped self head; accepted: lexicographic (col0 LT, or col0 EQ then col1 LT), literal rebuild S{p} off S{S{p}}, joint multi-column match, accumulator after the shrinking column, Nat-fuel-driven HOAS evaluation.
facts.quote: bend has no opt-out, so the runnable half of the bend3 test has no place in this file

facts.claim: Halt tests pin that the structural wall is the substitute for a positivity check: non_structural_field.bend (Ord with Sup{g: Nat -> Ord}) refuses rec(g(0n)) and says 'bend has no positivity check; this wall is the guard'; strict_descent.bend refuses mk(x) under a minted Sup (run confirmed, exit 1); unguarded_decrement.bend refuses f(Nat.sub(d, 1n)) (run confirmed).
facts.quote: bend has no positivity check; this wall is the guard

facts.claim: Halt tests: a bare self-reference as a value (def a(): a at Type; def bad(): bad at {Nat == D : Type}; def loop(): a => loop(a)) is refused as non-decreasing, so recursive equality proofs cannot justify casts and type-level self recursion is rejected before conversion can loop.
facts.quote: recursive equality proofs cannot justify casts

facts.claim: Stuck corpus (26 files) pins the evaluator: a call applied to a constructor prefix over a free variable unfolds through the prefix and stays stuck as a call (never an exposed match); the checker accepts all. Runs confirmed: ack.bend --check-only prints ALL PROOFS CHECK and run prints 'x => 1n+ack(1n, x)'; sum.bend run prints 'x => 3n+add(x, 2n+add(x, 1n+add(x, sum(x))))'; ack.bend --verdict with kernel prints 'ALL PROOFS CHECK' exit 0.
facts.quote: An evaluator that unrolled the stuck call's arms would never stop here

facts.claim: README Limitations state: recursion must terminate and @unsafe or def f?(..) turns the check off; values are affine (closures and arrays cannot be shared); F32 is axiomatic; the checker has no proof and may have bugs while --verdict uses a proven kernel; the compiler (not kernel) is 99% AI-written.
facts.quote: The checker has no proof and may have bugs; `--verdict` uses a proven kernel.

facts.claim: README CLAIMS a stronger guarantee than the code gives: 'it is mathematically impossible to break laws in LAWS.bend. The compiler enforces it' and 'Bend's compiler then guarantees that these laws always hold'. The code conditions this on: the proof being complete (no TODO), no @unsafe/foreign taint (only reported by --check-only/--verdict, not by a run with main), and the elaborator translating the law faithfully.
facts.quote: it is **mathematically impossible** to break laws in `LAWS.bend`

facts.claim: WONTFIX: the checker skips dead code (an unused let/beta argument, a shadowed arm, a fallback past the last constructor) and a written redex reduces as read so (x => x(x))(x => x(x)) never ends; the termination check reads arguments left to right; the checker is not optimal (exponential cases, machine-stack recursion); an unbalanced Array tree and a Nat past 2^48-1 fail-stop at runtime though the theory admits them.
facts.quote: The checker visits neither. This makes the check faster and costs no correctness: the term it checks is the term it runs.

facts.claim: WONTFIX carve-outs touching soundness: a base-file helper may call a law filled below it ('User files do not get it'); handle types (File, Socket, Window) are laws only Base may leave unfilled, and 'Opening this to user files touches consistency'. WONTFIX says 'the Lean formalization states it', but bendtt.lean contains no occurrence of 'base' or 'carve' (grep -i); laws go out to the kernel as 'opaque' defs checked against a model.
facts.quote: A base-file helper may call a law filled below it (#793) `base.bend` carries this carve-out and the Lean formalization states it.

facts.claim: AGENTS.md: bend.ts is human-written and not to be edited; bendtt.lean is the kernel with claims 'no checked def has type Empty, live code halts' and their proofs; --verdict builds its CLI once with Lean v4.34.0; every test ends in the #| lines its run must print.
facts.quote: its claims (no checked def has type Empty, live code halts) and their proofs

facts.claim: bendtt.lean states the kernel's Claims formally: Claim.consistent (no def of a checked book has a type convertible to <>), sound, confluent, sr, progress, halts, empty; the file has zero 'sorry'. The proof route: dead parts are never run or measured so 'A dead region may hold Girard's paradox'; 'Type : Type is harmless, since nothing here asks a type to normalize'.

facts.claim: bendtt.lean live rule as stated: the live part of a def must be affine, may call only earlier defs, and may call its own def only on parameters it rebuilt, then a piece of one; a q=2 binder needs a Data domain and Data holds no λ and no call.
facts.quote: may call its own def only on parameters it rebuilt, then a piece of one. A q=2 binder needs a Data domain, and Data holds no λ and no call.

facts.claim: safe.ts (the elaborator from the checked bend2 book to BendTT text) is outside the proven kernel; a def with no body goes out opaque at a model; what the kernel cannot express is out of scope and --verdict fails; GUIDE says 'the translation has no proof, so read it to confirm a law'.
facts.quote: the translation has no proof, so read it to confirm a law

facts.claim: GUIDE documents the LAWS.bend/PROOF.bend convention: LAWS.bend imports the code and states the laws (human-written); PROOF.bend imports LAWS.bend and proves each law with a def of the same name (law sorted is proven by def Laws.sorted); bend PROOF.bend prints SOME PROOFS FAIL while any law is open or false; bend refuses a PROOF.bend beside a LAWS.bend that does not import it; a law left open in one file may be filled in another as def M.name(..).
facts.quote: bend refuses a `PROOF.bend` that sits beside a `LAWS.bend` without importing it.

facts.claim: GUIDE on @unsafe and ordering: termination is mandatory and mutual recursion is not allowed; an @unsafe def recurses freely and may call a def below it but 'a check prints SOME PROOFS FAIL and names every def that relies on it'; types are not code so datatypes may name each other in any order.
facts.quote: `bend` runs it, but a check prints SOME PROOFS FAIL and names every def that relies on it

facts.claim: Templates (~ binders) are the only higher-order escape from affinity: a ~ argument must be closed and checks dead in the empty context; the instance k~n is minted and checked at first live call; an instance is not in book.order so it is 'no claim'; instance nesting is capped at 64 levels and a ~ argument key at 32768 chars.
